event.summary: Removed stream negotiation leaves old pages requiring reload
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: A page left open across the grid-only upgrade can draw grid records as terminal text until reloaded. Source: assigned 01039-001.patch removes capability-negotiation tests and stream notices; SPEC_impl.md:3009-3030 explicitly defines protocol 77 and this compatibility boundary. Exact acceptance: 'A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working.' It further says: 'Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy.' Contract and source agree: the changed tests now exercise a single grid wire format, not a missing optional capability. Suggested bucket: other; could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route (malformed old-page input ends the attachment under this contract). Confidence: confirmed from source and specification, no execution. proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance quoted above. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: this decision concerns removed negotiation and changed tests only, not the entire terminal migration owned by other groups.

event.summary: Check fallback decoder against systemctl's actual literal grammar
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04ffdbb35773cef36e73eb798c005ddbeb9a9de6. TLDR: If systemctl emits shell literals outside this decoder's finite grammar, container probing could refuse the host or copy the wrong proxy value when busctl is unavailable. Source: units.rs:557-570 parses each assignment and decode_manager_value (664 onward) handles whole raw/single/double/ANSI-C quoted values, not concatenated shell words. Caller podman_probe.rs:337-371 falls back from busctl and decodes all entries before selecting proxy variables. SPEC_impl.md:6561-6565 requires deterministic proxy inheritance from the place host's user-manager environment. Suggested bucket: other pending establishing an actual emitted value and consequence; could-be-highest: no established route, and no shell evaluation occurs. Confidence: unresolved lead, not a reported bug. Checks made: read full assigned decoder patch and fallback caller; exact missing premise is the actual shell-literal output grammar of supported systemctl versions. Next check: primary systemd source for show-environment and its quoting helper; it can settle whether concatenated literals or other unsupported forms are produced. proposed_drop: false while investigating. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Fallback decoder covers the checked systemctl literal grammar
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04ffdbb35773cef36e73eb798c005ddbeb9a9de6. TLDR considered: a wrong fallback parse could make containers unusable or copy the wrong proxy value when busctl is unavailable. Checks and results: read the assigned full decoder patch and podman_probe.rs:337-371; checked primary systemd v239 systemctl.c:5127-5140 and escape.c:432-474, plus v252 and v255 systemctl-set-environment.c:42-54 and v255 escape.c:440-518 / escape.h:13-26. show-environment quotes only the value using ESCAPE_POSIX/SHELL_ESCAPE_POSIX. It emits a raw whole value or one whole ANSI-C quoted value, not concatenated shell words. v239 escapes apostrophes/backslashes and tabs/newlines; the newer helper also C-escapes control bytes and keeps valid UTF-8. The decoder covers these produced forms. Primary refs: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v239/src/systemctl/systemctl.c#L5127-L5140 ; https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v239/src/basic/escape.c#L432-L474 ; https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v255/src/basic/escape.c#L440-L518 ; https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/v255/src/systemctl/systemctl-set-environment.c#L42-L54 . SPEC_impl.md:6561-6565 requires deterministic proxy inheritance. Suggested bucket: other for the considered failure; could-be-highest: no security or work-loss route established, parsing never evaluates shell text. Confidence: confirmed refutation of the suspected grammar mismatch for these versions, source-only; not a claim to exhaustively validate all historical systemd versions. proposed_drop: source refutation above; no emitted unsupported literal was found. possible_cover: none. Lead closed to candidate; no unresolved premise remains for the specific concatenation/escaping suspicion.

event.summary: Retired-session TCP admission may rely only on the durable cache
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR suspected: a retired container session may still open a tunnel to its former outside host when there is no durable cached payload. Source basis: tunnels.rs:303 and 361 now use route_active_session; sessions.rs:4527-4550 routes normally then refuses only from store.cached_session. resolve_owner:935-960 allows membership via status.live_sessions when no cache exists. Download, attach, and upload supervisor paths have require_active_launch, but a targeted check of service/tcp_relays.rs found only store membership at 278-279, no require_active_launch call. Missing premise: whether a shipped connected status can retain a retired live session without a durable cached payload, and whether the TCP route is genuinely the terminal tunnel endpoint in that case. Next: read tcp_relays.rs admission and identity-less listing publication/caller contracts. Suggested bucket: other until material consequence established; could-be-highest: potentially accesses outside-host services instead of the retired container, but no security impact or shipped route yet established. Confidence: unresolved lead, source-only; no runtime execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false pending investigation. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched.

event.summary: Retired-session TCP cache gap has no established shipped route
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR considered: a retired container session without a durable cached payload could still open a tunnel on its former outside host. Source checks: sessions.rs:904-960 admits membership from a cache key or identity-less status.live_sessions; route_active_session:4527-4550 examines only the durable decoded payload. store.rs:9719 onward returns None for missing/corrupt/mismatched payload. Supervisor service/tcp_relays.rs:264-286 checks only that a row exists before connecting loopback, unlike the checked file/terminal/upload paths. Thus the API-level gap is real for a constructed identity-less peer or damaged cache. Investigation of manager.rs:4366 onward establishes why this does not yield a shown normal shipped route: 'NOT an old supervisor: one predating PLAN_M6.md item 2 speaks an older protocol version and is refused at the hello gate long before this, so what actually lands here is a construction with no standing to mint one (a test peer, an embedded supervisor built without a state directory to claim from).' The manager's ordinary identity-bearing path caches the complete typed listing before it becomes visible (refresh code 4893-4990), and route membership without such a listing refuses. No shipped cause of a retired row's cache payload becoming corrupt or mismatched was established. SPEC.md:4816-4823 says existing retired sessions support Delete only. Suggested bucket: other for an API/constructed-peer contract gap, with no material user consequence established. could-be-highest: considered outside-host service access, but neither an unintended security boundary crossing nor a shipped route is established; full-authority desktop tunnel calls and existing consent are still required. Confidence: source-confirmed checks and absence of established production premise, not an execution observation. proposed_drop: no established shipped trigger; identity-less routing is explicitly limited by the cited source to embedded/test constructions, and cache corruption is only hypothetical. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Lead closed to candidate; the precise premise that would reopen it is a supported production path that exposes a retired session without its decodable durable cache payload. A source caller or retained production cache evidence would settle that premise; no reproduction was made.

event.summary: Bounded refutation of ordinary retired-session TCP cache bypass
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR considered, preserved: a retired container session lacking a decodable durable cache payload can authorize a TCP tunnel on its former outside host instead of being Delete-only. The constructed API gap remains real: sessions.rs:4527-4550 checks only store.cached_session after route_session, store.rs:9719-9795 returns None for bad/missing payload while raw paired membership still routes, and supervisor service/tcp_relays.rs:264-286 checks only row existence before dialing loopback. client/tcp_relays.rs:327-369 confirms this is the BeginTcpRelay path used by tunnels.rs:303,361. No live-state/view/attachment guard is substituted for that distinct TCP boundary.

Contract check: the complete pinned SPEC_impl.md Rootless Podman sessions section (8642-8657) says 'A retired session supports Delete only. Refuse all other lifecycle, terminal and exec paths, including plain Replace.' This is a global retirement requirement. It does not explicitly prescribe an independent retirement check at each supervisor endpoint. event.summary: Clipboard writes are split below the grid frame bound and reassembled
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR considered: an 8 MiB program clipboard write might be dropped by the surviving 1 MiB grid message limit before it reaches the enlarged native route. Source investigation refutes that interaction. The complete relevant grid clipboard format paragraph, crates/farhelm-proto/src/grid.rs:226-236, explicitly says a write longer than one message is split into contiguous parts, at most GRID_MAX_CLIPBOARD_PART_BYTES of text and within GRID_MAX_MESSAGE once encoded; only the whole write has the 8 MiB cap. Constants at :413,459,463 distinguish 1 MiB encoded frame, 512 KiB raw part, and 8 MiB total. Supervisor grid_output.rs:946-981 implements both part constraints, counting escaped JSON size and cutting at character boundaries; service/grid_stream.rs:786-790 appends every part and sends them in order. The helm gauge's 1 MiB frame admission (client.rs:837-844) therefore admits each encoded part independently. UI grid-model.js:1042-1065 checks 512 KiB per part and 8 MiB across parts, collects text and publishes it only on last; grid-terminal.js:1982-1983 forwards that completed text to onClipboard. The assigned clipboard.rs test starts at this completed-text boundary, so its direct route POST is a valid test of the route cap; it need not itself exercise the separate splitting protocol. rest_harness.rs:829-833 uses the real build_router and middleware, not a cap-bypassing test handler. Suggested bucket: other for the considered cap/test-premise issue. Could-be-highest: no; no security or user-owned-work-loss consequence established, and the priority rules exclude clipboard content itself. Confidence: confirmed source/contract refutation, no runtime observations or reproductions. proposed_drop: source-refuted bound mismatch; 8 MiB is a whole-write bound while 1 MiB is per encoded part, with checked splitting and reassembly. possible_cover: none; supplied interface context was read only for novelty and prohibited coverage sources were not searched. Lead closed to candidate; no missing premise remains for this specific interaction.
